stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Flegler move likely; Cowboys keen to keep Nanai
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1. Isaac Issa has news from the Dragons on some key outside backs
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Flegler move looking likely
Tom Flegler is looking likely to leave the Dolphins at the end of 2027, with ESPN understanding the prop is leaning towards a move away from the club.

While Flegler is yet to make a firm decision, the Dolphins are now facing the prospect of losing him for the 2028 season and beyond.

His future shapes as a situation to watch as the November 1 contracting window approaches.

Cowboys keen to keep Nanai
North Queensland remain keen to retain Jeremiah Nanai, with ESPN understanding the Cowboys are hopeful the back-rower will extend his stay despite preparing to test his value on the open market from November 1.

Nanai has been with the club since he was a teenager, developing into a Queensland Origin representative, and the Cowboys are hopeful that connection will help keep him in Townsville.

Samrani expected to test open market
Jordan Samrani is expected to test the open market from November 1. ESPN understands he will explore his options for 2028 and beyond.

Following a breakout season with the Parramatta Eels, Samrani is open to assessing opportunities elsewhere when the contracting window opens on Sunday.

Cochrane set to link up with Titans feeder

Taye Cochrane is set to link up with Gold Coast Titans feeder club Ipswich Jets for the 2027 season following his departure from Canterbury.

ESPN understands the young fullback has signed with the Queensland Cup outfit after the Bulldogs opted against offering him a contract for next season.

Cochrane scored six tries in 14 NSW Cup appearances for Canterbury in 2026, having been part of the club's Jersey Flegg premiership-winning side in 2024.

The move follows Phil Gould's confirmation that Cochrane would leave the Bulldogs, with ESPN revealing he had not been offered a new deal.

Bulldogs opt against Cochrane deal

Canterbury have opted against offering Taye Cochrane a contract for 2027, with the young fullback set to depart Belmore.

ESPN understands Cochrane was not offered a new deal, following Phil Gould's confirmation he would not remain at the Bulldogs next season.

Cochrane scored six tries in 14 NSW Cup appearances this year, playing predominantly at fullback.

He was part of Canterbury's 2024 Jersey Flegg premiership-winning side before progressing to NSW Cup the following season.

Panthers make retention intentions clear on Patea
Penrith have informed Luron Patea's management of their desire to retain the young prop beyond 2027, although he still intends to test the open market from November 1.

ESPN understands multiple clubs are interested in speaking to Patea, who is approaching the final year of his Panthers contract.

ESPN previously reported that Penrith had yet to begin extension discussions with Patea.

Tigers keen to retain Mason

Wests Tigers are keen to retain Heath Mason, with the club working through roster space to accommodate the young utility.

ESPN understands Mason remains part of the Tigers' long-term plans, although his future is yet to be resolved ahead of 2027.

Cowboys open to keeping Taumalolo

North Queensland are open to retaining Jason Taumalolo beyond 2027, with the veteran forward's assessment of how his body is holding up set to guide the next step.

ESPN understands the Cowboys will take their lead from Taumalolo as he weighs up his playing future, reflecting his standing as a club legend.

Taumalolo is contracted until the end of next season and becomes eligible to negotiate with rival clubs for 2028 onwards from November 1.

Panthers lock in Patea
Penrith have secured Tua Patea until the end of 2029, with the youngster signing an extension that includes a pathway from a development contract into the club's top 30.

Patea capped off the 2026 season with a hat-trick in the Panthers' Jersey Flegg Grand Final victory, having started the year with an NRL training block.

The new deal will see him join Penrith's full-time NRL squad as he works towards a first-grade debut.

Bulldogs closing in on Skelton return

Jeral Skelton is closing in on a return to Canterbury following his departure from the Wests Tigers.

ESPN understands the Bulldogs are in advanced discussions to bring the outside back to the club for the 2027 season.

An agreement is understood to be close, although the deal has yet to be finalised.

Multiple NRL sides eye Knights forward

A Sydney club and a Queensland-based club are monitoring Newcastle forward Mat Croker ahead of November 1.

ESPN understands the two clubs have shown interest in the 27-year-old, who is approaching the final year of his Knights contract and can negotiate with rivals for 2028 onwards from next month.

Rivals keeping tabs on Dragons' Tu

Multiple clubs are monitoring St George Illawarra outside back Setu Tu, with the Dragons yet to begin talks over a contract extension.

Tu is contracted until the end of 2027 and is expected to test the open market from November 1, when rival clubs can negotiate a deal for 2028 and beyond.

The former Warriors outside back joined the Dragons on a development contract this season and is set to move into the club's top 30 squad in 2027.

His ability to cover multiple positions across the backline adds to his appeal as clubs assess their recruitment options.

Roosters eye Dockar-Clay reunion
The Roosters have shown interest in a potential return for Zach Dockar-Clay as they explore options to bolster their hooking and utility depth.

ESPN understands the 31-year-old has emerged as an option following his departure from Manly, with discussions remaining at an early stage.

Dockar-Clay spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons with the Roosters before joining the Sea Eagles on a one-year deal for 2026.

Manly confirmed his departure last month after a season in which he claimed the club's NSW Cup best-and-fairest award.

Bostock brushes Dragons links

Dolphins star Jack Bostock has dismissed recent links between himself and the Dragons, admitting this isn't the first time he'd been floated for a club switch.

"I've been linked to a few a clubs," Bostock admitted.

"I don't know about [the Dragons links]."

He said that while he "obviously sees it in the media," his sole focus is the Kangaroos.

Sloan's Dragons stay still a possibility

Tyrell Sloan could yet remain at St George Illawarra next season, with discussions ongoing over a potential stay despite his planned move to Castleford.

There is interest in keeping Sloan at the Dragons, but several hurdles remain before that can become a reality.

Roster space and salary cap room would need to be worked through, while any arrangement would also require Castleford to agree to release him.

Sloan previously admitted he would "love to" remain in the NRL when speaking to Channel Nine in August, after his Castleford deal had been announced.

No agreement has been reached and a stay is far from guaranteed.

stories.headline: Brewers let Game 4 slip away as Rays send World Series to a Game 5
stories.summary: The Brewers were three outs away from their first World Series championship but the Rays stormed back in the bottom of the 12th inning Tuesday night to force a Game 5.
stories.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- When Cooper Pratt led off Tuesday's 12th inning, he was just trying not to strike out. Instead, he hit the home run that gave his Milwaukee Brewers the lead and put them three outs away from their first championship.

He had become the first 22-year-old to accumulate four hits in a potential World Series clincher, and he was on the precipice of becoming a savior in Wisconsin.

"That was probably one of the coolest swings of my life," Pratt said, "but it's over."

Actually, when it comes to this World Series, it's not. It's not because the Tampa Bay Rays stormed back in the bottom half, putting the first five baserunners on to win Game 4 in walk-off fashion, 4-3, and avoid a sweep. It's not because the Brewers lost their first postseason game in 21 days. It's not because the Rays would not go down without a fight.

As the Brewers dominated October, winning 10 of their first 11 games and tying a record with eight consecutive victories, it was at times easy to dismiss the difficulty of what they're pursuing.

Not for their players.

"This stuff is not supposed to be easy," Brewers captain Christian Yelich said. "It's supposed to test you."

The biggest test presented itself to Shane Drohan, a journeyman rookie who hadn't pitched in 12 days. He was summoned from the bullpen after Brewers third baseman Joey Ortiz made an errant throw to begin the bottom of the 12th, putting the tying run on, and couldn't help but think about what three more outs might mean.

"I'm human," Drohan said. "I know what I was walking into, and I just didn't get the job done."

The first batter Drohan faced, Liam Hicks, hit a hard ground ball to the left side that would have been a double play if Pratt weren't shaded closer to second base to defend against a left-handed hitter. Instead, it went through, putting runners on the corners with none out, bringing the infield in and significantly ratcheting the degree of difficulty.

The next batter, Jonny DeLuca, lined a base hit up the middle, tying the score. Chandler Simpson did the same, loading the bases. And then pinch hitter Ben Williamson hit a chopper so hard it sailed over the head of first baseman Jake Bauers, found the outfield grass and handed the Brewers only their second loss all month. Moments later, Drohan was asked what makes him believe his team could overcome it.

"Because we've done it all year," Drohan said. "We've been the best team in baseball all year."

The outcome might have been different with a little batted-ball luck. The Brewers produced 12 of the 13 hardest-hit balls of the night. Nine of them exceeded 102 mph and went for outs. It might have also been different had Ortiz completed a routine play by throwing accurately to first base on Junior Caminero's grounder.

"I should make that play every f---ing time," Ortiz said.

But he didn't. And the hits didn't fall. And -- for one night, at least -- the Rays proved superior. The Brewers had claimed 18 straight victories when leading at any point in a game, dating to Sept. 17, tied for the longest single-season streak in franchise history, according to ESPN Research. Now, if they're going to secure the first championship, they're going to have to show more perseverance.

Maybe that's how it's supposed to be.

"It's going to be hard," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said. "When you're achieving something like this, it's going to have its adversity."

stories.headline: Fantasy football confessional: Seven draft-day lessons to file away for 2027
stories.summary: With the fantasy regular season halfway over, ESPN Fantasy analysts explain their biggest takeaways thus far.
stories.body:
In life and in fantasy football, it's a good idea to assess and adjust as you go, even if you can't apply what you've learned until a later time.

Internalize the lesson while they're fresh, is what we're saying.

Now that we have reached the halfway point of the fantasy regular season, we asked our ESPN fantasy football analysts to highlight one of the lessons they've learned this season.

These takeaways will eventually guide future draft strategies and decisions, and some may even apply to lineups right now as we all move away from our Los Angeles Chargers, but the common thread is that even the experts are constantly learning.

You need a proven back for the "hero RB" draft strategy
If you are building your strategy around a specific player, it is best to know that player can carry a team. I like the hero RB approach, in which you take one running back early and then wait before taking your second one as you get your starters at every other position. But I learned a tough lesson this year, as I went with Omarion Hampton as my hero RB in too many leagues and it has been a struggle at the position each week.

My teams where I went hero RB with James Cook III, Jonathan Taylor or Ashton Jeanty (or two RBs early) are doing much better. That's especially the case with it becoming more difficult to find usable RBs off the waiver wire. Or, maybe the lesson is don't trust a Charger. -- Michael F. Florio

That second RB can be a hero, too (see: Kenneth Walker III)

I was looking at some of my better teams and it's no surprise the teams where I drafted in the top two seem to be doing much better. That feels like a no-brainer because those teams have either Jahmyr Gibbs or Bijan Robinson, both of whom have been excellent this season.

But the other common thread is that I took a second back early: Kenneth Walker III. Bypassing the hero RB strategy and loading up with Walker has proven to be quite a benefit, especially when ignoring other receivers who were available in those slots. In other words, it was the old-school RB-RB approach that really did it for me. -- Adam Rank

You really don't need that "tier one" quarterback in the draft
We talked about the depth at the QB position all offseason, and that's really bearing fruit through the first half of the season. Jared Goff, Caleb Williams, Brock Purdy, Bryce Young and Trevor Lawrence are all top-10 QBs in fantasy PPG this season, while Kirk Cousins, C.J. Stroud, Tyler Shough and Matthew Stafford each have at least three games of 20-plus fantasy points this season.

You didn't need to use an early draft pick on a QB, and in today's pass-heavy league, that trend may continue heading into next year. -- Daniel Dopp

The new coaching hire doesn't always lead to immediate results
I was all-in on the Chargers this offseason after the club hired Mike McDaniel as the new offensive coordinator. The system fits here, no? More two-back personnel. A heavily schemed run game. Defined throws for the quarterback. So, I pushed both Hampton and Justin Herbert up my draft board because of it.

But as we enter Week 8, this offense has been a bust. Hampton is scoring just 9.6 fantasy PPG and Herbert has fallen completely out of my weekly ranks (and we rank 25 QBs). Now, there are always other factors here, like the subpar play of the Chargers' interior offensive line, for example. It's rough. Still, this is a good reminder that coaching moves can require a transition period, which will directly impact player production.-- Matt Bowen

If you're going to settle at tight end, just stream

Brock Bowers (19.1 fantasy PPG) and Trey McBride (18.6) are dominating in a tier of their own, proving well worth their early-round ADP. Later-round picks Isaiah Likely (16.1) and George Kittle (14.9) provided better preseason value, while Tyler Warren (14.0) is the only other tight end to crack the top five.

Ultimately, this production curve proves that instead of settling for middle-tier traps like Colston Loveland, Kyle Pitts Sr. or Harold Fannin Jr., the best positional strategy is to either invest in elite talent early or hunt for value late. -- Liz Loza

Just because a player hasn't done it before, doesn't mean he can't do it
I admit I was skeptical of Walker handling a massive workload with the Chiefs and delivering MVP-type numbers. Walker's career high for touches in a season as a Seahawk was a modest 255 during his rookie campaign. Today, through six games, he is on pace for 391 touches, and there is little evidence the Chiefs plan to alter the trend, nor can they afford to do so.

Walker missed games in three of his four previous seasons, and I scoffed at the possibility of him approaching 400 touches with his new franchise. Today, who knows? Perhaps I will be more trusting of potential workload increases for running backs in future seasons. -- Eric Karabell

Be supremely patient through proven players' September struggles
We're all sorry, Drake Maye. After three weeks of sub-10-point fantasy production, we were all running for the hills. Since then? He's scored 23-plus in four straight and is QB3 for the season. Maye did look awful in September, posting the league's worst interception rate (7.5%). He also faced three defenses (@SEA, PIT, @JAX) that, for the season, rank among the eight toughest against quarterbacks (schedule adjusted).

Remember, we don't really know anything about the intricacies of the matchups themselves during the opening weeks. We need to give them evaluation time, and we need to face the possibility that our struggling players may be dealing with bad matchups. So, will I forgive Maye for getting me ousted in the opening week of our in-house Knockout league? Yeah, I guess I will. -- Tristan H. Cockcroft

stories.headline: NBA Power Rankings: How all 30 teams stack up after one week
stories.summary: Here's where all 30 NBA teams rank after one week of the 2026-27 regular season, plus the most surprising statistic or trend for each franchise.
stories.body:
It's been a little over a week since the start of the 2026-27 NBA regular season, and we've already had a jam-packed couple of days filled with surprise starts, star returns and a few disappointing debuts.

LeBron James kicked off his 24th season with the new-look Philadelphia 76ers by defeating the defending champs -- the New York Knicks -- after their ring ceremony at Madison Square Garden and displaying early positive returns following a busy offseason.

On the flip side, the San Antonio Spurs, after a Finals appearance in June, are struggling behind young superstar Victor Wembanyama. However, their cross-state rivals, the Houston Rockets, are one of four undefeated teams left in the Western Conference, along with the Oklahoma City Thunder (the 2024-25 champions), the Memphis Grizzlies and the Portland Trail Blazers.

In our first iteration of Power Rankings this campaign, our NBA insiders break down their biggest observations from opening week, including the most surprising statistic or trend for every team, and what to expect as teams try to find their footing or build on their momentum.

Note: Team rankings are based on where members of our panel (ESPN's Jamal Collier, Michael C. Wright, Tim MacMahon, Dave McMenamin, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Ben Golliver, Kris Rhim and Anthony Slater) think teams belong.

Previous rankings: Preseason

Jump to a team:

ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE

DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND

LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN

NO | NY | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX

POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS

1. Oklahoma City Thunder

2026-27 record: 4-0
Previous ranking: 1
Next games: @ DAL (Oct. 28), @ HOU (Oct. 31), @ CLE (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: Third-year guard Ajay Mitchell's elevated role. In the wake of the serious injuries suffered by Jalen Williams (fibula/ankle) and Cason Wallace (shoulder), Mitchell should see an increased role on the floor. He has repeatedly shown that he can thrive as the No. 2 offensive option alongside two-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. Mitchell averaged 22.5 points and 6.0 assists in the Thunder's sweep of the Lakers in last season's Western Conference semifinals, when Williams was sidelined. Mitchell had a career-high 30 points and five assists in Monday's win over the Suns, his first start of the season. -- Tim MacMahon

2. Minnesota Timberwolves

2026-27 record: 3-1
Previous ranking: 5
Next games: vs. GS (Oct. 28), vs. LAC (Oct. 30), @ SA (Oct. 31), vs. MIL (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: 120.8 offensive rating. Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball's instant chemistry was marvelous: Minnesota's new-look starting lineup outscored opponents by 31 points in 56 minutes through four games. Meanwhile, the Timberwolves posted a 120.8 offensive rating when their dynamic guard duo shared the court -- an exceptional mark that would have ranked second in the NBA last season. However, that could all come to a halt as Edwards will be sidelined up to two months, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Tuesday because of an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee. -- Ben Golliver

3. Detroit Pistons

2026-27 record: 3-1
Previous ranking: 7
Next games: vs. CHA (Oct. 28), @ BKN (Oct. 30), @ CHA (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: 42%. That's what the previously anemic Pistons have shot from 3 in the first three games this season. Duncan Robinson leads the league in makes per game (5.0) and is shooting a blistering 54% from distance, while newcomer John Collins is taking nearly five a night at a 50% clip. Last season, this team was barely near the league average and struggled at creating and making shots in the playoffs, leading to their second-round loss to Cleveland. Head coach J.B. Bickerstaff said Robinson is more comfortable looking for shots and taking contested ones, which also means some regression to the mean will occur. But being more aggressive is a positive sign of sorts. -- Vincent Goodwill

4. Houston Rockets

2026-27 record: 4-0
Previous ranking: 10
Next games: @ MIL (Oct. 28), @ DAL (Oct. 30), vs. OKC (Oct. 31), vs. BOS (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: 4-0 start. For the first time since 2014-15, Houston is off to a 4-0 start and finally playing the way it was expected to last season when it first acquired Kevin Durant. The return of veteran point guard Fred VanVleet, who missed last season with a torn ACL, has played a role in Durant starting off the season with four straight 20-point games for the 10th time in his career. Meanwhile, big man Alperen Sengun is feasting off the order VanVleet has restored to the offense, becoming just the third Rocket to put together multiple 25-5-5 games within the first four games of the season. -- Michael C. Wright

5. Philadelphia 76ers

2026-27 record: 3-1
Previous ranking: 4
Next games: @ IND (Oct. 28), vs. NYK (Oct. 30), @ CHA (Oct. 31), vs. CHI (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: 8.8. The Sixers averaged 8.8 offensive rebounds per game. As the Sixers struggled to rebound in the preseason, coach Nick Nurse wasn't concerned. "We're going to be a good rebounding team," he said then. The Sixers still aren't, ranking 29th in the NBA in offensive rebounding per game and 26th in total rebounds per game. The struggles make some sense as the Sixers front court has been decimated with injury, but it remains concerning and something Nurse is hoping they fix quickly. "I think that our guys understand that we gotta do a better job," he said. -- Kris Rhim

6. Los Angeles Lakers

2026-27 record: 3-1
Previous ranking: 11
Next games: @ LAC (Oct. 28), @ GS (Oct. 30), vs. TOR (Nov. 1), vs. MIA (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: 60/60/90. Austin Reaves got off to an unbelievably hot start through the Lakers' 3-0 showing out of the gates, averaging a career-best 26.7 points on 63.9% from the field, 61.5% from 3 and 89.7% from the free throw line entering Tuesday's game. He and Luka Doncic (34.3 points per game) are the only pair of teammates in the top 10 in scoring in the league. They would be even more effective if they took care of the ball better. They also both rank in the top 10 in turnovers per game through three games, with 7.0 for Doncic and 4.3 for Reaves. -- Dave McMenamin

7. Toronto Raptors

2026-27 record: 2-1
Previous ranking: 12
Next games: vs. ORL (Oct. 28), vs. ORL (Oct. 30), @ LAL (Nov. 1), @ LAC (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: 0-12. The Raptors' only loss this season came with Leonard sidelined, but Toronto will be without Leonard for a period of weeks as he manages left knee soreness. The concerning part about life without Leonard is that in the Raptors' first look without him, Scottie Barnes had one of the worst outings of his career, finishing 0-12 with three turnovers and a team-worst minus-27 in the 117-94 loss. -- Rhim

8. Boston Celtics

2026-27 record: 3-1
Previous ranking: 6
Next games: vs. CHI (Oct. 30), @ ORL (Nov. 1), @ HOU (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: Jordan Walsh is in the starting lineup. Starting Walsh, a rotational player who started 25 games last season, came as a bit of a surprise with veterans such as Sam Hauser and Payton Pritchard on the roster. But so far, Walsh's defense has buoyed the Celtics early in the season, slowing down guards including the Knicks' Jalen Brunson (2-for-7, five points against Walsh) and the Pistons' Cade Cunningham (1-for-3, three points against Walsh), according to NBA.com. -- Rhim

9. San Antonio Spurs

2026-27 record: 2-2
Previous ranking: 2
Next games: @ UTAH (Oct. 28), vs. MIN (Oct. 31), vs. UTAH (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: 1-2 start. The Spurs ran into the combustible mixture of growing pains in trying to evolve their offense with a new starting five while facing two of the West's toughest teams -- Oklahoma City and Houston -- to start the season. So, the early struggles weren't unexpected, and the Spurs are comfortable with taking their lumps early. But in the process of trying to raise its ceiling, San Antonio lowered its floor, a disturbing early trend. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said, "We've got to just keep getting back to the standard we know we are capable of. Our floor right now is way too low." -- Wright

10. Portland Trail Blazers

2026-27 record: 3-0
Previous ranking: 17
Next games: vs. MEM (Oct. 29), @ UTAH (Oct. 31), @ DEN (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: 21-0 start. The Blazers enjoyed the perfect start to the intriguing Damian Lillard and Ja Morant partnership thanks to a blowout win over the Suns in their season opener. Portland raced out to a 21-0 lead in front of a raucous Moda Center crowd that eagerly welcomed Lillard back from an Achilles injury. Though Morant opened the season as a starter, he has had to make great sacrifices to fit into Portland's crowded backcourt rotation. The two-time All-Star is tracking toward career lows in minutes, points, shots and usage rate. -- Golliver

11. Indiana Pacers

2026-27 record: 2-2
Previous ranking: 13
Next games: vs. PHI (Oct. 28), @ MIA (Oct. 30), vs. BKN (Nov. 1), vs. ATL (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: 21.8. The number of points Tyrese Haliburton is averaging through his first four games back from injury. He has scored at least 20 in three of the first four games of a season for only the second time in his career, played in a back-to-back this week and he's averaging 9.5 assists. Any worries about him needing to ease back into action have been unfounded. Haliburton looks like his old self after missing 16 months, but the Pacers are going to need to get healthier around him (Ivica Zubac has a sprained left ankle, T.J. McConnell has yet to play in a game in either preseason or regular season and Ben Sheppard tore his meniscus). -- Jamal Collier

12. Denver Nuggets

2026-27 record: 1-2
Previous ranking: 8
Next games: @ NO (Oct. 28), @ PHX (Oct. 30), vs. POR (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: The Nuggets' 119.3 defensive rating is fifth worst in the league. It's been a strange first homestand for the Nuggets. They fell 23 points to the Pelicans and even received some boos, but then stormed back for an overtime win with help from rookie Trevon Brazile, who made a handful of spectacular plays and looks like a second-round steal at a time Denver desperately needs depth. After the game, Nikola Jokic called out the jeering fans, saying they weren't welcome back, and doubled down a couple nights later after they were blown out at home by the previously winless Warriors. -- Anthony Slater

13. Cleveland Cavaliers

2026-27 record: 2-1
Previous ranking: 9
Next games: vs. WAS (Oct. 28), @ ATL (Oct. 29), @ MIL (Oct. 31), vs. OKC (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: Keep an eye on the wing trio of Peyton Watson, Sam Merrill and Jaylon Tyson and how they complement Cleveland's core four throughout the season. That trio has made just 19.5% of their combined 3-pointers so far -- but it's still very early, so there's plenty of time for those role players to turn it around and start making more shots in support of the stars. -- Zach Kram

14. Memphis Grizzlies

2026-27 record: 4-0
Previous ranking: 24
Next games: @ POR (Oct. 29), vs. SAC (Oct. 31), vs. NO (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: Ty Jerome's hot start and the Grizzlies 4-0 start. Memphis' 4-0 start ranks as the second best in franchise history behind the 2014-15 campaign in which the Grizzlies won their first six games. Perhaps the most eye-popping early trend comes from the way this young team has performed in clutch time. Three of Memphis' first four outings turned out to be clutch time games, with the Grizzlies winning all of them to tie the 76ers for the most clutch wins so far this season. Jerome ranks third in the league in scoring (29.8 points per game) after a career-high 45-point season opener, which he then followed with 31 points against the Kings. -- Wright

15. Atlanta Hawks

2026-27 record: 2-2
Previous ranking: 15
Next games: vs. MIA (Oct. 28), vs. CLE (Oct. 29), @ NO (Oct. 31), @ IND (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: Can Quin Snyder continue to rely heavily on his rotation? One storyline entering the season was whether the Hawks' frontcourt could succeed against quality opponents. The loss at Houston proved they have a long way to go. In the ten-point loss, Atlanta was outrebounded 40-22 on the offensive glass (52-35 overall) and were minus-11 in free-throw attempts. The lone frontcourt player with a positive plus-minus was Onyeka Okongwu. Through the first four games, nine players have averaged more than 18 MPG, with only starter Jalen Johnson averaging more than 30 MPG. -- Bobby Marks

16. New York Knicks

2026-27 record: 1-3
Previous ranking: 3
Next games: @ CHI (Oct. 28), @ PHI (Oct. 30), vs. BKN (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: 30th. That's what the Knicks ranked at in both offensive efficiency and raw scoring entering Tuesday's game. It's a small sample size, but the Knicks have barely shown more than flashes of that potent offense. "We get a little comfortable," Jalen Brunson said after Sunday's loss to Orlando, in which New York gave up 40 fourth-quarter points to the Magic. Before Tuesday, Mikal Bridges registered donuts at the foul line and 3-point line. One is expected, the other is not.-- Goodwill

17. Charlotte Hornets

2026-27 record: 3-1
Previous ranking: 23
Next games: @ DET (Oct. 28), @ WAS (Oct. 30), vs. PHI (Oct. 31), vs. DET (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: 36.3 PPG. New Hornets Grayson Allen and Naz Reid came to Charlotte in trades for Miles Bridges and Ball, respectively, and both sharpshooters are excelling in their new digs. Allen and Reid have combined to average 36.3 points per game while making 44% of their 3-pointers, and both players rank in the top 10 in the NBA in made 3s. -- Kram

18. Washington Wizards

2026-27 record: 2-2
Previous ranking: 22
Next games: @ CLE (Oct. 28), vs. CHA (Oct. 30), @ ORL (Nov. 2

Most surprising stat or trend: 8.8 PPG. After averaging 16.3 points per game with a 26% usage rate in a promising sophomore season, Alex Sarr is down to 8.8 PPG with a 14% usage rate this year. That decline epitomizes the difficult balancing act for the Wizards as they try to win games with veteran stars Trae Young and Anthony Davis, while also providing opportunities for their many prospects to develop on the court. -- Kram

19. Phoenix Suns

2026-27 record: 1-2
Previous ranking: 18
Next games: vs. DEN (Oct. 30), @ GS (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: 40. Devin Booker recorded the 40th 40-point game of his career with 43 points on 17-for-25 shooting in the Suns' 131-122 win over the Warriors opening week. It's the most in franchise history, with Amare Stoudemire trailing significantly behind at No. 2 with 15 of them. Phoenix is off to a slow start, however, with Booker combining for just 26 points on 8-for-20 shooting in the Suns' other two losses. -- McMenamin

20. Orlando Magic

2026-27 record: 1-2
Previous ranking: 16
Next games: @ TOR (Oct. 28), @ TOR (Oct. 30), vs. BOS (Nov. 1), vs. WAS (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: 3. Injuries are forcing Orlando to utilize its third starting lineup in four games when it plays Toronto on Wednesday. Former All-Star Paolo Banchero is out indefinitely with an ankle injury, while Jalen Suggs will miss at least two weeks due to a bone bruise in his right knee. Injuries have impacted them in the last two seasons, with Banchero and Franz Wagner playing only 64 games together in that span. -- Marks

21. Utah Jazz

2026-27 record: 1-3
Previous ranking: 20
Next games: vs. SA (Oct. 28), vs. POR (Oct. 31), @ SA (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: Ace Bailey stepping up during early Jazz injuries. Utah's frontcourt has been ravaged by injuries, as Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee), Lauri Markkanen (wrist) and Jusuf Nurkic (toe) are all sidelined. Second-year forward Bailey's performance has been a silver lining during the Jazz's rough start. Bailey, the No. 5 pick in last year's draft, has back-to-back double-doubles, averaging 17 points, 11 rebounds, 3.5 assists and two blocks in the two games. -- MacMahon

22. Dallas Mavericks

2026-27 record: 2-2
Previous ranking: 21
Next games: vs. OKC (Oct. 28), vs. HOU (Oct. 30), vs. SAC (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: Cooper Flagg's disruptive abilities. Flagg's disruptive defensive tendencies were as much of a factor as his offensive potential in scouts and executives considering him one of the best draft prospects in a generation and those skills have been on display early this season. Flagg leads the league with 3.7 steals per game and ranks in the top 20 in blocks (1.7). He had five steals and three blocks during his 29-point, 11-assist masterpiece in Monday's win in Miami. The only other teens to ever record at least five steals and three blocks in a game: Kevin Garnett and Wembanyama, both of whom went on to win a Defensive Player of the Year award. -- MacMahon

23. LA Clippers

2026-27 record: 1-2
Previous ranking: 27
Next games: vs. LAL (Oct. 28), @ MIN (Oct. 30), @ GS (Nov. 1), vs. TOR (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: 26.3%. That is Rui Hachimura's field goal percentage through his first three games with the Clippers after signing a two-year, $28 million contract to move from Crypto.com Arena to the Intuit Dome in the offseason. The dip in efficiency comes off a season when he shot 51.4% for the Lakers -- the second-best clip of his career -- and raised his level to 54.9% in the playoffs. Hachimura only had 11 games last season out of the 68 he played where he shot under 30% for the game. He's done that in two out of his first three games with the Clippers. -- McMenamin

24. Miami Heat

2026-27 record: 0-4
Previous ranking: 14
Next games: @ ATL (Oct. 28), vs. IND (Oct. 30), @ LAL (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: 105.3. We won't compare this current iteration of the Heat to Miami's inaugural team in 1988-89, which lost 17 straight games. But like their first team, the current roster is only the second team in franchise history to start the season with four straight losses. The lack of success derives from an offensive rating that ranks 27th (105.3) and a defensive rating that sits at 24th (118.8). One trend to watch is whether Miami can improve from the perimeter. The Heat rank 25th in three-point percentage and have no player besides Portis Jr. and Davion Mitchell shooting greater than 35%. -- Marks

25. Chicago Bulls

2026-27 record: 1-3
Previous ranking: 26
Next games: vs. NYK (Oct. 28), @ BOS (Oct. 30), @ PHI (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: 25.5. That's the number of minutes Josh Giddey is averaging per game in what has been an underwhelming start to the season. On opening night, Giddey revealed he injured his left wrist and will have to manage the injury all season. Both his production -- 7.0 points and 7.3 assists on 33% shooting -- and playing time have dipped as a result, and the Bulls offense has sputtered out of the gates. Entering Tuesday, they had the worst offensive rating in the league through four games. -- Collier

26. New Orleans Pelicans

2026-27 record: 0-3
Previous ranking: 25
Next games: vs. DEN (Oct. 28), vs. SAC (Oct. 29), vs. ATL (Oct. 31), @ MEM (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: 23-point collapse. Jamahl Mosley is still seeking his first win as coach after New Orleans inexplicably blew a 23-point lead to Denver on Saturday. The Pelicans might regret their stumbles out of the gate: The NBA handed them a soft early-season schedule, playing nine of their first 13 games against teams that missed the 2026 playoffs. Mosley has started 2025 lottery pick Jeremiah Fears, but the guard's abysmal shooting -- 29% from the field and 18.2% from deep -- has been a real drag on the Pelicans' offense. -- Golliver

27. Golden State Warriors

2026-27 record: 1-3
Previous ranking: 19
Next games: @ MIN (Oct. 28), vs. LAL (Oct. 30), vs. LAC (Nov. 1), vs. PHX (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: It couldn't have been a louder opening week to a career for Yaxel Lendeborg. After getting in a public dust-up with Doncic (they face each other again on Friday), the rookie wing went on a statistical binge, becoming the fourth player since 1986 to compile at least 85 points and 35 rebounds in his first four games. Shaquille O'Neal, Patrick Ewing and David Robinson are the other three. It didn't take long for him to earn Steve Kerr's trust. Lendeborg put away the Nuggets on Monday night with Stephen Curry on the bench and Kerr said afterward, "He's going to be a guy who closes games." -- Slater

28. Milwaukee Bucks

2026-27 record: 1-3
Previous ranking: 29
Next games: vs. HOU (Oct. 28), vs. CLE (Oct. 31), @ MIN (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: Zero. That's the number of minutes Gary Trent Jr. has played for the Bucks this season despite signing a four-year, $64 million contract during the offseason. The deal confused several team executives around the league when it was agreed upon, and those questions have only increased as Trent -- the fourth-highest-paid player on the roster -- can't even crack the rotation. At least Milwaukee has avoided having a zero in the win column after a win against Indiana on Monday, dodging what would have been the Bucks' first 0-4 start in 50 years. -- Collier

29. Brooklyn Nets

2026-27 record: 0-4
Previous ranking: 28
Next games: vs. DET (Oct. 30), @ IND (Nov. 1), @ NYK (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: Julius Randle has been efficient, despite the losses. If there was any notion that Randle would be a selfish star coming into a Nets team stuck at the bottom of the standings, it has been anything but. He kept them in their first two games -- which were respectable losses to Charlotte and Cleveland -- and led them to an overtime loss against the Celtics on Tuesday night. He leads the Nets in scoring (22.0), rebounding (7.0) and assists (6.3) while shooting over 50% from the field and 45% from 3. For a team that will struggle to score all season, having Randle aggressive will at least keep this young team in games. -- Goodwill

30. Sacramento Kings

2026-27 record: 0-4
Previous ranking: 30
Next games: @ NO (Oct. 29), @ MEM (Oct. 31), @ DAL (Nov. 2)

Most surprising stat or trend: As expected, rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. has received the greenest of lights. He attempted 24, 26 and 23 shots in his first three games, surpassing Durant for the most shots three games into a career in the modern era. But the Kings received concerning news regarding their other wing asset, as small forward Keegan Murray will miss at least the next two weeks while dealing with stiffness in his surgically repaired left ankle. It has been bothering Murray throughout training camp and he hasn't been moving well to open the season. He is in the first season of a five-year, $140 million extension. -- Slater

stories.headline: Arteta, Alonso, Iraola: Three Premier League managers all come from one tiny club
stories.summary: Whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or World Cup, hiring a coach from Spain's northern coast is bringing clubs guaranteed success.
stories.body:
There is irresistible evidence right now that signing coaching talent from Spain's northern coast brings guaranteed success, and Arsenal, Liverpool, Aston Villa and Chelsea need no convincing.

In international terms, the European and world champions (Spain) are coached by a Basque (Luis De La Fuente), in club terms, double Champions League winners PSG dance to the tune of another north-coast Spaniard, Luis Enrique, and the reigning Europa League holders and English champions owe their success to a couple of guys, Unai Emery and Mikel Arteta, who grew up within a few miles of one another in San Sebastián (part of the Gipuzkoa territory in Spain's Basque country).

It is, literally, a phenomenon. This is a coaching domination by a small community on a grand scale.

Now the fascinating prospect is that four of England's great clubs will all be jostling for trophies and bragging rights this season, in the Premier League and in Europe, under the control of coaches who all learned at one amateur Gipuzkoa football club on the Bay of Biscay coastline.

Arteta, Emery, Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso have already enjoyed jaw-dropping coaching success -- historic triumphs with Arsenal, Bournemouth, Bayer Leverkusen, Sevilla and Aston Villa between them. Now, they will all be going toe-to-toe for England's silverware.

What they also share, particularly Arteta, Iraola and Alonso, is an identical development path, often criss-crossing experiences in their home town of San Sebastián, being trained under the same ethos, often by the same coaches.

The amateur club in question is Antiguoko, which can claim partial responsibility for Bournemouth earning their first ever UEFA qualification (Iraola played for Antiguoko as a kid then, eventually, began his coaching career there), for Bayer Leverkusen winning their only Bundesliga title (Alonso) and for Arteta bringing Arsenal their first Premier League trophy in 22 years. Remarkable, right?

Those who run football at Antiguoko, and around the Gipuzkoa region, are beginning to smile with resignation as Europe's media approach them and demand the magic formula which has produced these brilliant alumni (and a host of other key figures in coaching and directorial roles around the continent).

There's no magic -- just ideology, hard work, decades of development and attention to detail.

Iraola says: "The number of successful coaches formed in the Basque Country receives a lot of attention because, despite being a small place, we have a great football culture."

When Arteta was last asked about what it is that makes Basque coaches so successful he gave a simple, short answer: "It's about passion we have and the education that we all got."

That education includes the fact that kids who follow the Arteta-Alonso-Iraola route in Gipuzkoa, aren't allowed to belong to a single club, practising a single sport, until they're 10 years or older.

The idea being that young boys and girls must continue to learn and develop through other sports like basketball, handball and volleyball before they, eventually, specialise.

The concept is to keep mixing with differently talented youngsters, to keep working on different spacial and athletic disciplines, to learn from and then cross-fertilise eclectic ideas.

Written down in black and white it makes simple sense, doesn't it?

There is also a huge emphasis placed on the coaches who train kids earning good qualifications, having a shared ideology, and being given respect by the community around them.

Again, doesn't that sound like basic common sense and decency?

During research for this column, Manu Diaz, the president of the Guipúzcoa Football Federation, explained: "There's a disproportionate number of coaches in our region because of our sense of community -- people want to give something back.

"Kids want to become coaches, they wait for their 16th birthday to be able to start doing their badges as if they were waiting for the chance to learn to drive. You also learn from a young age how to be part of a big group and that lends itself to eventually being good at leading. The coach is very well respected.

"People can invent a narrative that there is a common school of football here but really more than a shared way of seeing the game, it's a shared way of seeing life. There's a Basque word that sums it up: 'Auzolan' which refers to working together with neighbourly cooperation."

Some of that is evidenced by the way in which Arteta, Alonso, Iraola and co. learned their earliest football skills, and learned "neighbourly cooperation" via the phenomenon particular to San Sebastián where huge numbers of junior football matches are played on the two main beaches.

When the tide is out, parents, kids and coaches literally draw out a series of pitches on the flat, hard La Concha and Ondarreta sand, drag out stored goal-frames and play dozens of matches until the Cantabrian sea sweeps in again.

The pitch-lines need to be scraped out by hand in the sand. Speed and teamwork is of the essence -- not just when the matches start but in joining together to create the massive jigsaw of 10, 12, or 15 pitches as quickly as possible so that a host of games, with boys and girls of all ages, can take place. Teamwork makes the dream work.

Alonso, who won his first-ever trophy with Arteta in a tournament with Antiguoko when the pair were barely in their teens, explains: "I was lucky enough to have Mikel, who was also crazy about football, in our neighbourhood. Every day we'd go down to the beach on our skateboards to play tennis, surf, and, of course, play football."

There's no getting away from the fact that the Basque school of football development uses phrases and ideology which the modern, money-obsessed, fast-paced, hard-nosed elite world of football would find hokey and old-fashioned.

Perhaps that's the key: All the things that drive old-school fans crazy, that make them feel detached from the modern, foreign-owned, exorbitantly priced, corporate and investment-fund football are the opposite to the Antiguoko, Gipuzkoa, Basque ways which gave us Alonso, Arteta, Iraola and Emery.

"It shines a spotlight on one of European football's premier youth academies," an Antiguoko spokesperson told ESPN. "We are a neighbourhood institution -- modest in resources yet colossal in influence. We have served for decades as a true school for both footballing and human development.

"These guys who now work in the Premier League have publicly acknowledged the profound impact Antiguoko K.E. had on their athletic and personal development. We nurture players, by fostering raw talent, but also via a culture of hard work, tactical intelligence, game interpretation, and collective commitment.

"A footballing philosophy grounded in competitiveness and holistic development. Our club embodies the very essence of local grassroots football. Here, football is in the air from a very young age -- but so, too, are discipline, a sense of closeness, and a deep feeling of belonging."

Five years ago Alonso was one of the co-authors of the Real Sociedad training manual, "Made In Gipuzkoa" published to help anyone across global football who cared to read it, learn from it and apply the concepts.

One of its key phrases, again sounding from another age, is: "The essence of this model is the person, not just the footballer."

The training manual continued: "That boy or girl whose future we don't yet know -- footballer, engineer, doctor, mechanic, lawyer -- is the centre of everything. In this model, each person is a project in themselves, and everything else revolves around them.

"Coaches at Real Sociedad accompany, nurture, and train the boys and girls throughout their entire journey, with stability as the foundation of a model based on trust and patience. In short, to nurture, to train, to guide, to educate. That is the mandate we receive from the community we want to represent, from the families of Gipuzkoa, from Gipuzkoa society in general."

From that old-fashioned, humanistic, community-based football philosophy to the cutthroat, high-tech winner-takes-all ebb and thrust at the top of England's Premier League.

Whatever divides Alonso, Emery, Arteta and Iraola this season, they are all unified by background, beliefs and some values that all of European football could learn from.

stories.headline: Why Devin Cooley is the most interesting man in hockey
stories.summary: His postgame quotes have become the stuff of legend. Here's what teammates, coaches and others have to say about him.
stories.body:
CALGARY -- It has become almost routine.

Calgary Flames goalie Devin Cooley turns in a stellar performance, earns a live postgame interview and turns what's normally a cliché-ridden exercise into a soliloquy on modern sports psychology as seemingly the entire sports world tunes in.

Cooley's gems of late? First there was this on Oct. 18:

"The problem with me is that I have a lot of fun playing, but when I start having too much fun, it [takes] me from an unconscious goalie to a conscious goalie, and my conscious brain is really bad at playing goalie. I have to let my unconscious brain do the work, because it reacts a lot quicker."

And then a week later:

"I feel completely in control of my mind ... whatever my mind throws my way, I feel I'm in a good state to handle. ...Even when I go home. I go home, and I'm not really thinking about much. I'm just reading with my rabbit and not thinking about much."

Cooley was named the NHL's second star of the week ending Oct. 25, and his quotes offer a rare glimpse into the mind of an elite athlete -- and perhaps the most interesting man in hockey.

COOLEY HAS A PET RABBIT, Tito, and learns linear algebra in his spare time. Before this season, he had already gone viral when, as a relatively unknown (and undrafted) backup goalie for the San Jose Sharks two years ago, he famously told media, "Nothing's really gonna matter. We're all gonna die."

Dr. Michael Gervais is one of the world's preeminent high-performance psychologists. He hosts the "Finding Mastery" podcast, interviewing the likes of Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, and author Malcolm Gladwell. He has worked with the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks and a host of other organizations.

Dr. Gervais is also, like the rest of us, captivated by Cooley.

"I would love to have a conversation with him about how he organizes his life and his internal life to find the freedom and the joy and the absolute highest expression of performance," he said.

Dr. Gervais explained that Cooley has found an optimal flow state where he can perform without his brain getting in his way.

"The conscious mind is incredible for learning. ... It's how you gather feedback, it's how you correct and adjust," he explained, but, "it's a terrible place to perform from, because when we're thinking, we're not responding. ... If you're consciously thinking about where your glove should be, you're absolutely already late."

That, Dr. Gervais explains, is Cooley's advantage. The athletes he has worked with are in that flow state about 20% of the time. Cooley, it seems, is in his flow state for far longer. "You can train your conscious mind to trust your non-conscious," Dr. Gervais said. That includes the drills that Cooley does in practice to work on different facets of his game that he might use when the bright lights come on.

"Most performers, they get in trouble not because they lack skill, but because they think and overthink and then all that thinking crowds out all the automatic responses they've built for maybe two decades."

Former NHL goalie (and now mental performance coach) Mike Condon joked that he wished he'd had Cooley's approach during his own 129-game career. Beyond his pro credentials, Condon has a master's degree in clinical mental health counseling. His outlook in his playing days was very different as he suited up for the Montreal Canadiens, Pittsburgh Penguins and Ottawa Senators.

"You don't need to be confident in order to play well," he said. "I never felt confident before any game. I never thought anything was going to go well. ... For me, it was all about courage, so facing fear and doing it anyways. If I had that, then I would be fine."

He explained that there are different approaches. For some clients, tools such as affirmations and positive imagery work.

"What Devin's doing [is] he's putting out another roadmap on the mental game other than just, 'Think positively,'" he said.

THOSE WHO KNOW COOLEY aren't totally surprised by his recent success (and fame). Cooley's first pro coach was Brad Ralph with the ECHL's Florida Everblades during the 2020-21 campaign.

"He asked a lot of questions, you could tell he was an intelligent guy," Ralph recalled.

"One time I walked on the bus, and he was pecking away on his laptop, and I looked at his screen, and it was some next-level algorithm-type coding whatever. You could tell he's a smart guy."

Of course, Cooley can also play -- and well.

He was an unheralded free agent signing by the Flames two years ago. Since then, the Los Gatos, California, native has risen from projected AHL starter to essentially platooning with Dustin Wolf. Last season, Cooley was one of the league's breakout performers with a 0.909 save percentage. It earned him an invite to the 2026 IIHF World Championship.

This season, he has continued his strong play and earned four consecutive starts for Calgary, where he has developed under goalie coach Jason LaBarbera, a longtime pro goalie and former NHLer. In that stretch, Cooley has a 1.50 goals-against average and 0.955 save percentage.

"He really had no plan [when we signed him]," LaBarbera said. "He was basically playing off feel. ... He's a big guy, but he can move. He's an athlete, [and has] ability to react and recover when he needs to, and be big and patient when he needs to."

LaBarbera and Cooley's teammates love those postgame clips.

Defenseman Joel Hanley said the two have gotten into some deep philosophical conversations over dinner. Veteran Ryan Strome said Cooley adds an element of joy to the team. "I appreciate a guy that exhausts all ideas and options to get there," Strome said.

"He comes to the rink, and he kind of says, 'Look at what we get to do for a living.' I think he's always got a smile on his face. That type of attitude is super infectious. ... For me, the biggest thing is that he works hard, he loves winning, he loves competing, and that's my favorite trait in a teammate."

Condon sometimes shows Cooley clips to the younger goalies he works with.

"When you're in the tunnel before you go out in the game is probably the most vulnerable mentally that you're going to be of accepting where you are and where you're supposed to be at," he said.

"If you're there with these expectations that, 'I need to feel this way, I need to feel that way in order to have success,' you're going to put yourself into some psychological difficulty."

Condon added, however, that Cooley won't quell certain stereotypes about the position.

"We're not weird," he said. "We just have a very, very uncomfortable environment that we have to learn to cope with and it's fun to see how different people do that. Devin's one of those people."

stories.headline: Mexico City Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Formula 1 heads to Mexico on a weekend where Kimi Antonelli could win the drivers' championship for the first time.
stories.body:
Formula 1 heads to Mexico on a weekend where Kimi Antonelli could win the drivers' championship for the first time.

The Mercedes driver extended his lead in the title to 123 points from George Russell after winning the United States Grand Prix. He will simply need to finish ninth or higher in Mexico City to seal the title.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was looking strong in the upgraded Ferrari to finish second in Austin, with Max Verstappen on the final step of the podium.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 19th round.

- How Kimi Antonelli can win F1 title at Mexico GP -- with or without Qatar, Abu Dhabi races

Practice Two: 10 p.m. - 11 p.m.

Final Practice: 5.30 p.m. - 6.30 p.m.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Mexico City Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez
Mexico City is one of the most vibrant atmospheres on the calendar and fans congregate in the thousands to cheer on home hero Sergio Pérez.

It's a true anomaly on the calendar due to the high altitude of of 7,300 feet (2,200 metres) and therefore presents a unique challenge for the teams and drivers. Teams can run Monaco-level downforce packages while still reaching Monza-esque top speeds.

One of the iconic parts of the track -- the Foro Sol stadium section -- includes two tight corners in a former baseball stadium.

2015: Nico Rosberg (Mercedes)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 1963

Laps: 71 laps of 4.3km

Lap record: 1:17.774, Valtteri Bottas (2021)

Most wins: Verstappen with five (2017-2018, 2021-2023). Other winners from the current grid are Hamilton (2016, 2019), Sainz (2024) and Norris (2025).

Most poles: Jim Clark with four (1963-1965, 1967). Other pole sitters from the current grid are Hamilton (2016), Leclerc (2019, 2023), Verstappen (2022), Sainz (2024) and Norris (2025).

Weather forecast

The weather for the Mexico City Grand Prix is set to reach temperatures of 27°C for qualifying and Sunday's race, with no rain due.

What happened last time out?
Norris pulled out a thrilling lap to take pole position in Mexico, his first pole since the Belgian Grand Prix in July. The Brit said on the team radio afterwards "What a lap. What a lap. Even I don't know how I did that."

It was a dominant race weekend from the McLaren driver after he became the new leader in the title race ahead of his teammate Oscar Piastri for the first time since April.

He had a one point advantage over Piastri with just four races to go.

Who will win this year?

Antonelli put his Mercedes on a surprise pole in Austin and converted it into another victory as he inches closer to taking the title crown with five races remaining.

The youngster will need just two points this weekend, or for Russell and Hamilton to not win the race, to get the job done in Mexico.

Red Bull are a looming threat each weekend after bringing major upgrades and Verstappen will be one to watch out for. He's also got five race victories under his belt around Mexico City.

All eyes will be on Antonelli. He will be hoping to wrap up the title and is looking like he's in a position where nobody will be able to stop him.

stories.headline: Dream say concerns over finding available WNBA Finals venue went unheeded
stories.summary: In a letter to the city, the Atlanta Dream said Game 6 getting moved to 12:30 p.m. so they can play in State Farm Arena was "not what we fought for."
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- In an open letter addressed to the city, the Dream said concerns they had over the availability of a properly sized venue for WNBA Finals games in Atlanta went unheeded and that the solution of moving Game 6 up to 12:30 p.m. ET was "not what we fought for."

Game 6 between the Dream and Golden State Valkyries will be played Thursday at 12:30 p.m. as opposed to the originally scheduled 8 p.m. The shift in timing was a result of the game being moved to State Farm Arena, the home of the Atlanta Hawks.

The Dream have played all their home games this postseason at State Farm Arena, which seats roughly 17,000 fans. Their home court, Gateway Center, fits just 3,500.

To accommodate Game 6, the Hawks' home game against the Cleveland Cavaliers that night will move back one hour to 8 p.m. To accommodate Game 4 at State Farm Arena, the Hawks' home game this past Saturday was moved to 8:30 p.m. All three Finals games in Atlanta have required hurried adjustments to the schedule.

"As much as we have great affection and nostalgia for Gateway Center Arena, we believed that our fans and the city wanted the opportunity to be a part of this historic series, and to see it played on a world-class stage," the letter said. "That meant State Farm Arena."

In the letter, the Dream said they brought up concerns involving potential playoff scheduling and dates that overlapped with NBA games at the arena two months ago. The organization said that while it reiterated the issues as the playoffs went on, "our concerns did not receive the attention, nor the urgency that they deserved."

Sources told ESPN's Alexa Philippou that the dates for the 2026 playoffs were sent internally to teams on Dec. 4, 2025.

Negotiations between the WNBA, Dream, Valkyries, Hawks, NBA and broadcast partners took place over the weekend to figure out the best course of action for all parties involved.

The NBA and WNBA explored options to keep Game 6 in primetime, ESPN's Ramona Shelbourne reported. However, the Hawks and Cavaliers both play Wednesday night, so they could not play their game in the earlier time slot Thursday.

"I hope everyone gets to see it somehow, and I know for some people it's not realistic -- they have jobs and won't be able to make it," Dream coach Karl Smesko said ahead of Game 5 in San Francisco. "I'm disappointed for that, but I'm hopeful as many people as possible can see the game."

In a statement Monday, WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert added: "The sellout crowds and extraordinary atmosphere at State Farm Arena for Games 3 and 4 were a tremendous success, and we're excited to give thousands more fans the opportunity to experience Game 6 with a championship on the line. We thank the NBA, Dream, Valkyries, Hawks, State Farm Arena and USA Network for the collaboration and flexibility that made this move possible. We look forward to delivering another unforgettable Finals experience in Atlanta."

Valkyries players Kiah Stokes and Veronica Burton encouraged fans in the Bay Area to call in sick to watch the game, while their coach, Natalie Nakase, expressed confidence that Golden State fans would tune in from wherever they had to despite the 9:30 a.m. tipoff in California.

Dream players including Allisha Gray, Jordin Canada and Angel Reese brushed aside the game time as a nonfactor.

"It's the Finals," Gray said. "We just got to do what we've got to do. We are locked in on winning Game 6 whether it's 8 a.m., 10 p.m., midnight. We got a championship to win."

stories.headline: Nowhere to rise for Volkanovski and Yan, but Reyes and Volkov move up
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
Two of the greatest performances at UFC 333 earned no reward in ESPN's divisional MMA rankings.

Both featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski, who knocked out Movsar Evloev in Saturday's main event, and men's bantamweight titlist Petr Yan, who won a trilogy fight against Merab Dvalishvili in the co-main, were already ranked No. 1 in their divisions, so there was nowhere for them to rise in those top 10s.

Evloev, who lost for the first time in his career, and Dvalishvili, an ex-champ who dropped his second straight to Yan, maintain their No. 2 rankings.

Other fights on the Abu Dhabi card did affect rankings. Light heavyweight Dominick Reyes was the lone fighter to defeat someone ranked higher than him, knocking out sixth-ranked light heavyweight Azamat Murzakanov. Reyes moves from No. 7 to the top five, and Murzakanov falls to Reyes' former spot.

Heavyweight saw a trickle-down succession of movement, partly due to a fight result. Alexander Volkov, who beat unranked Rizvan Kuniev, moves up one position to No. 3, largely because former UFC champion Tom Aspinall, previously ranked second, has been removed from the top 10 as ineligible because he has not fought in over a year. The other ranked heavyweights each move up one spot, and Kuniev enters the rankings at No. 10.

The other ranking change is at men's flyweight, where Lone'er Kavanagh climbs one position to No. 6 after handing unranked Ramazan Temirov his first loss.
